note: The board's single data source. Rows carry states; TILE states are never stored — they derive at render by the pinned rule: a tile shows its most-blocking open row (to-clarify flag first, then waiting, then being built, then not reported, then not started; a tile whose rows are all unreported renders Not reported); a tile is done-and-checked only when every row is done. Milestones are rows of a milestone kind, in two classes: checked work, and observed world facts (source named). Vocabulary identical across prototype and shared versions; migration is a re-home of this file, not a re-entry of states. Schema v2 adds per-item watch targets and watch health; proposed changes live in board/proposals.json, never inside item states, and land only on a partner's tap. Standing requirement (Andy, 2026-10-24): the board surfaces things not documented yet — said on a call but never became an item · built but never claimed or recorded · decided but never written down — as proposed entries, which become items only on a partner's confirmation. Role (ruled by Andy, 2026-11-03): this board is the partner board system of record for cross-agent/system collaboration between the two partners' agent systems.

history.subject: product
history.text: The seven-room redesign (PF-9) landed on the deployed app: Home, Jobs, Tracker, Resume Studio, Documents, Targets & onboarding, and Settings recomposed in one shared grammar, each landing verified on the live deployment. Home's landing covers its composition, its briefing echo's spend behavior, and its briefing's line grammar; how Home's pieces read together on a return visit is a known open gap, named on the lane's record — the redesign is not claimed complete for Home beyond those three.

history.subject: register
history.text: Purpose, scope, and currency settled whole — five rulings on Andy's side: the market (quota-carrying sales roles, career transitions included); the promise (the product brings you the roles that align with where you've been and where you're going, and tells you exactly where you stand on each, kept current and true); the coverage standard (completeness inside the corpus, aligned roles per hunter per week, a zero-aligned guard); breadth-first sourcing (an aggregator becomes a primary source once its terms allow); and the closure standard for claims (built, landed, verified live, coherent).

history.subject: product
history.text: GK-6 ruled (Option 1, Andy's side): when a user's record changes, their affected scores re-score in the same act, silently; the count shows where the edit happened and movements surface as events on Home and the role's page. Ruled — not yet built.

history.subject: product
history.text: The daily ingest cure: the engine had never held the credential its own schedule required, so every supposedly daily cycle to date had been fired by hand. The credential was placed 2026-11-02; all 49 watched boards re-polled and about 260 stale postings were pruned. The cure's final proof landed the next morning: the first fully unattended cycle ran on schedule (2026-11-03, board stamps read direct from the store).

history.subject: product
history.text: The product's judgment, priced as an asset: naming the scorer, its matching rules, and its claim standards as one versioned 'hunt judgment pack' the engine loads, with a possible later door (MCP) that would let a user's own assistant import their hunt and work against the corpus and the pack. Priced and synthesized 2026-11-02/03 — not ruled, not built. The door awaits Andy's rulings on four points (a new surface class, any price on it, third-party access to a live hunt, and publishing the pack's internals).

history.subject: product
history.text: Two cures stand built and independently graded PASS, merge-ready, NOT yet live: the Home queue's 'New match' label now stands only on pairs that arrived since the last visit (it previously printed on a five-day-old pair beside a NEW counter at zero), and the Jobs page holds its matches frame from first paint so the tracked list never flashes at the top while the feed loads. They land on Andy's release with the next deployment batch.

history.subject: register
history.text: BOARD v1, ORDER 1 (THE FACE) LANDED (2026-11-03): the face re-shaped per Andy's corrected ruling. The board's views are kept, each simplified inside; shared components (ItemRow, DecisionCard, Stamp, FreshnessLabel, HistoryEntryLine) are each fact's one home; the overview is a composition of four routing segments (Needs a decision, Your move, Their move, Changed since you last looked); every number on the face is computed at render, the milestone line reading 2 of 8 from this record; History is wired and What changed derives from the history log, which the feed now carries whole. The build is verified at rendered strength from the board's code repository; the board's published face picks the new code up when the Studio project is next published, which is Andy's act.

The Stamp component now serves every surface that prints the stamp; FreshnessLabel serves the detail panel's row line; DecisionCard heads each gap card in Open questions. No derivation changed: the milestone line still reads 2 of 8 from this record, and the face's counts stand as landed at seq 43.

This satisfies the seq 43 statement: the new face is no longer only in the repos and the feed — it is what the address serves.

history.subject: register
history.text: BOARD v1, ORDER 2 (PROPOSALS + NOTES) LANDED (2026-11-03): the board now carries the partners' proposals and item notes as live machinery. Proposals live in their own data home beside this register and print on the board at their derived state (proposed, adopted, declined, with declines and their reasons shown); notes attach to items and print in the item's detail place. A checker guards every landing of either file, and the write repo's pull path stands ready: it has run once against the seeded repo and consumed zero writes, the seed's examples excluded by rule. The live sets are born empty, honestly: the first real proposal arrives through use. The same landing retired four components that no view mounted; the detail surfaces that remain carry the board's facts.

history.subject: register
history.text: BOARD ORDER 3a (PICKUPS AS ACTS) LANDED (2026-11-03): holding is now acts, not a field. Pickups, releases, and handoffs are entries in their own data home beside this register, and who holds what is derived from those entries wherever it prints — on the item itself in every view, and on the overview's pickup shelf, which lists what is held without counting either side's holdings. Two sides may hold one item (it prints as joined), a handoff passes a holding across, and a release closes only the holder's own holding, with its reason. This register's two claim fields became the first pickup entries, dated from the day they were actually claimed, and the fields themselves are gone: the fold over the entries reproduces the holdings exactly as they stood. A pickup of a proposal is its own act and changes nothing about the proposal's state.

history.subject: register
history.text: ORDER 3a PUBLISH VERIFIED LIVE (2026-11-05): the board's published face now carries the pickups build. The published copy was rendered end-to-end (fresh profile, the live feed fetched by the app itself): the stamp reads this register, the pickup shelf lists both holdings, and Your move reads 2 again. The same publish closed the interim skew the 3a landing had opened: between the register's migration (which removed the rows' claim fields) and this publish, the standing published copy — built from the earlier code — read holding from those fields and showed both moves at 0. The record was never wrong; the face was one publish behind, and the correction is on the landing records' faces.

Its state, at the strengths actually checked, is what both sides rely on. The October hold on sharing the board is lifted (Andy, 2026-11-03); the board is cleared to be shared with Tony.

The snapshot line is generated by the derivation from the register's own counts. Selection: the component tree and the standing principles cross whole; tiles, gaps, and rows carry their component and node keys and, from schema 2.5, their guide fields (blocked_by and couples_with edges, kind_of_work, watch_tags, and the decision-time how). The board renders this data and nothing else.
